answer: An agent marketplace requires every identity to lock $100 in a vault for 30 days before receiving one unit of bidding capacity. Agents named sparrow and sable each need their own bond, and splitting a bond across accounts creates no extra capacity. An attacker seeking 10,000 identities must therefore immobilize $1 million for a month, paying financing costs even if the identities earn nothing. Creating new names does not bypass the capital requirement.
